solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Compliment and regularly laud Slough

indicators.note: at regular intervals: every other letter

parts.note: the even letters of lAuD
a slough is a bog, a mire

explanation.surface: Someone praising and lauding the Berkshire town of Slough, not an obvious object of admiration.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London famous for being unlovely, and the capital hides its role as the plain noun for a bog.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: to compliment is to praise, and admire can mean to express admiration aloud.

clue.text: Reach home, full of love and aspiration

parts.note: ambit is scope or reach

indicators.note: the word for home is filled with the letter for love

parts.note: at home = in
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: Coming home full of love and hope: a happy homecoming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reach home' reads as arriving at the house, but it is two separate pieces: AMBIT, then I(O)N.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambition is aspiration, the desire to achieve something.

clue.text: Woman's focus: get rid of long whiskers

definitions.note: whiskers is plural; a moustache is a single growth of whiskers

indicators.note: the focus of a word is its centre letter

parts.note: the middle letter of woMan
to oust is to get rid of
to long for is to ache for

explanation.surface: A woman determined to remove some unwanted long whiskers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long whiskers' looks like one phrase describing the definition, but 'long' is the verb ACHE and only 'whiskers' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A moustache is the whiskers grown on the upper lip.

clue.text: Raving of guy on Ecstasy

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: to guy someone is to mock or rag them
E is the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A man ranting wildly while high on ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' is not a man here but the verb to guy, to tease, which is RAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Raving and rage both mean wild, furious talk or anger.

clue.text: "Dead end" clued as "bum, cold"

indicators.note: bum as an adjective means bad or faulty, so the letters are wrongly arranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters
C for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A setter admitting that the clue for 'dead end' came out as a bum, cold one.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue talks about itself: the words 'clued as' are the letters, and 'bum' is the adjective meaning dud, not the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym borrowed from French: a street closed at one end, literally 'bottom of the bag'.

clue.text: Opens sensual novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new form

parts.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.surface: Someone opening a steamy romance novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sensual novel' reads as a racy book; 'novel' is the adjective meaning new, telling you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To unseal something is to open it.

clue.text: Disconsolate old man wanting hugs

indicators.note: the outer word wraps its arms round the inner one

parts.note: wanting = desiring
your old man is your father, PA

explanation.surface: A lonely old man, miserable for lack of affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' looks like it means lacking, which fits the sad surface, but it is DESIRING, which hugs PA.
explanation.definitionFit: Disconsolate and despairing both mean without hope or comfort.

clue.text: Bottom of cavernous cistern smelt bad

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter

parts.note: last letter of cavernouS
a cistern is a water tank

explanation.surface: The bottom of a big old cistern gave off a foul smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom of' works because in a down clue the last letter sits at the bottom of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stank is the past tense of stink, to smell bad.

clue.text: Starts to cap abnormally square tooth

indicators.note: the starts of the next two words are their opening letters

parts.note: only the first letter of each word is used
nine is a square number, three times three

explanation.surface: A dentist fits an odd crown on a squared-off tooth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' is a noun here, a square number, rather than a description of the tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: A canine is one of the pointed teeth between the incisors and the premolars.

clue.text: Pester Head of History, a right idiot

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of History
as written
R for right
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A teacher badgering the Head of History, whom they think a complete idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of History' reads as a school job title, but it only gives the letter H.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to keep bothering someone.

clue.text: Sad person singing country music

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling sad
in British slang a grass is an informer, and to sing is to inform to the police

explanation.surface: A melancholy singer performing country music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person singing' looks like a vocalist, but in British criminal slang to sing is to inform, and an informer is a GRASS.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the banjo-and-fiddle style from Kentucky is one kind of country music.

clue.text: Cross about wife and kids

indicators.note: the first word goes round the second

parts.note: to span a river is to cross it
W for wife

explanation.surface: An angry man complaining about his wife and children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' sits in the surface as the adjective for angry, but it is the verb, SPAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Spawn is a disparaging word for offspring, a person's kids.

clue.text: See you in Egypt, at Aswan

indicators.note: the answer is inside the words that follow

parts.note: egypT AT Aswan

explanation.surface: A traveller saying goodbye somewhere in Egypt, at Aswan on the Nile.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma is only there for the surface; read straight through it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ta is an informal British goodbye, like see you.

clue.text: Barmy relatives providing element of slapstick

parts.note: going bananas is going mad
your kin are your relatives

explanation.surface: A mad family putting on some knockabout comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The split falls inside BANANA'S: the S belongs to BANANAS, not to SKIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipping on a banana skin is the classic slapstick gag.

clue.text: Liberal radicals probing extremely frustrating stealth tax

indicators.note: the rearranged letters probe, i.e. push inside, the outer pair
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: only its first and last letters are used

indicators.note: liberal suggests something free and loose, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Left-wing activists investigate a maddening hidden levy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks like a party label set against the radicals, but it is the anagram signal; a stealth tax is one that rises without being announced.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiscal drag raises the tax take without any change in rates, as inflation pushes incomes into higher bands, so it is a covert levy.

clue.text: Centre of Cork carpeted with small flowers

indicators.note: the centre of a four-letter word is its middle two letters

parts.note: the middle two letters of cORk
carpeted means told off; chid is an old past tense of chide
S for small

explanation.surface: A room in the middle of Cork carpeted and decorated with small flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpeted' means reprimanded (to be carpeted is to be summoned and scolded), and CHID is the old past tense of chide.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the orchid family is one of the largest groups of flowering plants.

clue.text: Season sprout well

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the season between winter and summer
second meaning: to sprout or shoot from the ground
third meaning: a natural source of water, like a well

explanation.surface: A gardener noting that seedlings shoot up nicely at this time of year.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions in a row: 'sprout well' reads as one phrase about thriving plants, but 'well' is the noun, a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers all three senses: the time of year, the verb to shoot up, and a natural water source.

clue.text: Audibly disparaged one exiting male toilet, active at night

indicators.note: the word is to be heard, not read

parts.note: to knock something is to disparage it
URINAL, a men's toilet, without I (one)

explanation.surface: Someone bad-mouthing a man leaving the gents during the night.
explanation.walkthrough: The male toilet is URINAL, and 'one' is the Roman numeral I, which leaves it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym phrased as a description, the way a dictionary glosses owls and bats.

clue.text: Austrian novice on slope

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a tyro is a beginner
to lean is to slope

explanation.surface: An Austrian beginner skier on the nursery slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slope' pulls towards the ski slope, but it is the verb, LEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tyrol is a region of Austria, so Tyrolean is Austrian.

clue.text: Bond's boss spies on monarch in old kingdom

indicators.note: in an across clue, placed after

parts.note: M is James Bond's boss
ER, Elizabeth Regina
the CIA, the US spy agency

explanation.surface: A spy chief keeping the king under surveillance in some ancient realm.
explanation.walkthrough: The spies come first in the clue but go second: 'on monarch' puts them after ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercia was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom in the English Midlands.

clue.text: Attack lieutenant south of Caribbean capital, not north

indicators.note: a down clue reads like a map with north at the top, so south of means placed underneath

parts.note: NASSAU, capital of the Bahamas, without N
Lt, lieutenant

explanation.surface: A military order: attack the lieutenant south of a Caribbean capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Nassau is the capital of the Bahamas; dropping its N (north) leaves ASSAU, with LT placed below.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, noun or verb: a violent attack, or to attack someone.

clue.text: Lauda broadcast on motor racing in particular

indicators.note: the name is heard over the air, not spelt

parts.note: Formula One, F1, with the 1 as I

indicators.note: in an across clue, placed after

parts.note: Niki Lauda, the Austrian racing driver

explanation.surface: Commentary on Niki Lauda, a famously meticulous Formula One driver.
explanation.walkthrough: Niki Lauda was a three-time Formula One world champion, so the surface is all F1. The 1 of F1 stands in as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Finicky means fussy, particular about details.

clue.text: Officers at law periodically left for holiday

indicators.note: every other letter is what is left after the rest go

parts.note: the even letters of oFfIcErS aT lAw

explanation.surface: Police officers taking time off for a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' does not mean the side; the letters left, once every other one is gone, spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiesta is a holiday or festival, especially in Spain.

clue.text: Ascending part of intestine containing last of enormous breakfast

indicators.note: the reversed word holds the single letter within it
in a down clue, ascending means read from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: the ileum is the last section of the small intestine

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: only its final letter is used

explanation.surface: A large morning meal works its way up through the gut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ascending' reverses ILEUM to MUELI, which holds S, the last letter of 'enormous'.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a mix of oats, nuts and dried fruit eaten as a morning cereal.

clue.text: Left in peace, played solemn duet

indicators.note: the letters are played in a different order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: Two musicians given peace and quiet to perform a solemn duet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Played' belongs to the musical surface, but here it tells you to rearrange the letters of 'solemn duet'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in its older sense: molest once meant simply to bother, so unmolested is undisturbed.

clue.text: Second balls-up in career

indicators.note: in a down clue, the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: balls is nonsense, ROT, turned upward
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A second blunder in someone's working life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balls-up' is British slang for a mess, but here it splits: balls is ROT, and 'up' turns it round. 'Career' is the verb, to rush along.
explanation.definitionFit: To career along is to speed along, to motor.

clue.text: Lord in court over game

parts.note: a British barrister addresses the judge as 'm'lud'
O for over, the cricket scoring abbreviation

explanation.surface: A judge presiding over a game in court.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six balls in cricket, abbreviated O on scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludo is a board game played with dice and counters.

clue.text: Characters leading open rebellion, chasing abominable whale

indicators.note: the characters that lead each word are the first letters

parts.note: first letters of Open Rebellion Chasing Abominable

explanation.surface: Rebel leaders in open revolt, hunting a monstrous whale, like Captain Ahab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abominable' nudges towards the snowman, but it is just another word supplying its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the killer whale is the largest of the dolphins, loosely called a whale.

clue.text: Half-cut saps finally get your goat

indicators.note: half of the word is cut away, leaving its first two letters

parts.note: only its first half is used

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word

parts.note: only its final letter is used

explanation.surface: Drunken fools end up irritating you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' is British slang for drunk, but here it cuts SAPS in half. 'Get your goat' means annoy, yet 'goat' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A satyr is a woodland creature of Greek myth, part man and part goat.

clue.text: Statement from unqualified civil engineer following article

indicators.note: the engineer comes after the article

parts.note: utter means complete, unqualified
an is the indefinite article
CE, civil engineer

explanation.surface: A statement issued by an unqualified civil engineer after an article about them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unqualified' looks like lacking qualifications, but it means absolute: UTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are something put into words.

clue.text: Irish capital both sides of the water

parts.note: Ir, Irish
Riga, capital of Latvia

indicators.note: the letters on each side of the word, its first and last

parts.note: first and last letters of ThE

explanation.surface: Dublin, the Irish capital, straddling the River Liffey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irish capital' looks like Dublin; it is two pieces, IR and a different capital, RIGA.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb, used of supplying fields with water through channels.

clue.text: Cycling along after drinking fifty eight pints

indicators.note: the cycled word, after drinking, has the numeral taken inside it
cycling moves a letter round from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A cyclist rides on after downing a huge quantity of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' moves the final G of ALONG to the front, giving GALON, which then drinks L.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallon is a unit of liquid volume; the imperial gallon holds exactly eight pints.
